required_interface: The finite Newton procedure checks the current residual before its correction budget, makes at most B corrections and B+1 residual evaluations, returns the last valid iterate with a root/singular-Jacobian/invalid-trial/budget status, and makes no arbitrary-start convergence or forward-error claim. A correction solves J s=-r when J is invertible.
evidence: Read the complete current batch-3 Definitions of alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals and alg-newton-correction-for-vector-residuals. The DAE wrappers retain their residual-first budget/status semantics and exact block correction; no convergence theorem is imported.

required_interface: Backward Euler solves the endpoint equation z-y-h f(t+h,z)=0. Its update residual is in state units and the derivative residual is the update residual divided by positive h. A residual is not a forward-error estimate without a separate inverse/stability bound; the endpoint definition itself grants no root existence or uniqueness.
evidence: Read the complete Definitions of def-backward-euler-step-equation and def-implicit-residual-and-algebraic-error-units. The DAE carriers use the same update/derivative units and enforce g=0 separately; their local residual-to-state estimate is proved in batch 75.

required_interface: For positive adjacent steps, the selected-branch algorithm uses the quadratic-interpolation BDF2 coefficients and requires exactly one root in a prescribed ball for its exact-root completion claim. The interpolation lemma gives an unscaled O(h^3) exact residual on a compact positive ratio interval; the constant-step specialization has ratio one. Batch 75's finite Newton status does not certify that exact selected root.
evidence: Read both actual batch-36 bodies and their complete arguments. Batch 75 uses the ratio-one coefficient/local-defect interface and separately proves the DAE branch, residual perturbation, and error recurrence.

required_interface: For h=T/N>0, a nonnegative sequence with e0<=C0 h^p and e_(n+1)<=(1+Lh)e_n+C h^(p+1) has a finite-interval O(h^p) bound, including L=0. Batch 75 applies p=1 to BE and p=2 to its BDF2 weighted-error recurrence.
evidence: Read the complete current batch-28 lemma Statement and Proof. The BE theorem establishes the recurrence locally; the BDF2 theorem first derives its weighted recurrence and then applies the supplier to N-1 steps over interval (N-1)h.
